## TL;DR

Added a responsive layout matrix to RepoOS's existing headless WebKit UI smoke test. It visits Work, Agents, Settings, Checks, Releases, and a task drawer at 375, 768, and 1280 CSS pixels. Every render checks document-level horizontal scrolling, clipping of visible primary buttons by the viewport or an overflow-clipping ancestor, and intersections between wide fixed bars. The check passed locally in 29.8 seconds and passed in the remote browser gate. No layout defects were detected in the seeded screens.

## Work and rationale

The implementation lives inside the existing `cmdUISmoke` browser harness. That harness already owns a short-lived preview fixture, starts the built app, launches WebKit headlessly, and classifies missing Playwright or WebKit as a clean skip. Reusing it means the new checks run as part of the established `smoke` script and therefore the `ui-smoke` check step. There is no new browser process, install requirement, or separate test command. The existing skip path remains responsible for optional browser dependencies.

The matrix uses the named `shotState` fixtures already used for preview captures: `pages:scroll` for Work, `agents:scheduledSeeded` for Agents, `settings:motionOff` for Settings, `checks:progress` for Checks, `release:cutReady` for Releases, and `drawer:reviewWithBranch` for the drawer. The drawer uses the seeded task id in the route. This provides stable populated content while exercising the screens people need to inspect, and avoids adding a second fixture system.

For each route and width, the page is sized before navigation and waits for the app root to render. The overflow assertion compares both `body.scrollWidth` and `documentElement.scrollWidth` to `window.innerWidth`. Visible primary buttons are selected by the established `.btn.primary` class or the explicit `data-primary-action` hook. Their bounds are compared with the viewport, then with ancestors whose overflow can clip content. Fixed-bar detection considers visible fixed elements spanning more than 55% of the viewport and with a bar-like height, then tests pairs for geometric intersection. Error messages identify the page, width, and relevant button or fixed element classes.

I also added a short engineering QA note and documented the behavior in the check guide. The docs describe the screens, viewport sizes, assertions, headless-only execution, command to run the smoke locally, and clean skip behavior. No `repoos.toml` change or runtime dependency was needed.

## Approaches tried

I first placed the responsive matrix before the existing smoke interactions, which seemed convenient because the browser page was already available. The next part of the smoke test then timed out looking for its server-seeded review task after the fixture-backed page visits. I tried explicitly loading a clean Work route after the matrix, but the following local smoke still timed out waiting for a page condition. The evidence pointed to unwanted coupling between fixture navigation and the existing interaction sequence, so I moved all matrix visits to the end of the smoke run, after the established interaction and console checks. That keeps the legacy smoke sequence independent and treats the matrix as a final read-only pass.

The first scoped check found a formatter issue in the new harness, so I ran `bun run fmt` and reran the requested scoped check. Subsequent full checks were needed after the smoke ordering changes. The final run completed formatting, lint, build, remote scoped tests, remote browser validation, local smoke, and the user docs build successfully.

## Challenges and blockers

The main challenge was preserving isolation in a long-running browser smoke test. Preview fixtures seed client-side state and can leave the browser on synthetic routes; placing them before an interaction scenario made that scenario unreliable even though the layout checks themselves were passing. Moving the matrix after the existing flows removed the ordering dependency. The optional browser slot was also occupied during one attempt, so the local smoke waited in the RepoOS queue before running; it eventually completed without issue.

One earlier check failed at formatting, and an intermediate smoke run failed on the existing review-task interaction. Both were addressed before the final pass. The final local smoke passed, and the remote browser gate reported success. The responsive matrix itself reported no overflow, primary-button clipping, or fixed-bar intersections, so this task did not identify a production layout bug that needed a CSS fix.

## Key learnings

The smoke harness is the right place for small deterministic page checks because it already handles fixture setup, headless browser ownership, teardown, optional Playwright behavior, and RepoOS's check integration. Existing shot fixtures provide broad populated states without maintaining duplicated test-only page data.

In a browser harness that combines direct route visits with interactive flows, fixture navigation should be ordered to avoid disturbing later scenarios. The final arrangement puts the new route matrix after interactions, so it is easy to extend while keeping the existing flow deterministic. The viewport matrix is also intentionally bounded: six screens at three widths, using one shared page and the existing fixture set. The measured local smoke duration was under 30 seconds, comfortably below the task's 60-second target.
